The postseason is here, bringing a compelling first-round matchup between the No. 7 seed Kentucky Wildcats and the No. 10 seed Santa Clara Broncos. Neither team currently sits inside the AP Top 25, but the stakes are high in this Midwest Region clash. Kentucky finished a volatile SEC schedule and now faces a tough test under head coach Mark Pope. On the other side, head coach Herb Sendek leads his West Coast Conference squad to their first tournament appearance since 1996. Watch Kentucky vs. Santa Clara on Paramount+. This game features an interesting storyline, as Sendek previously coached at Kentucky and actually recruited Pope. Analysts note the Broncos are a trendy upset pick against the eight-time national champions. If you want to catch every minute of this scheduled game, we have you covered. Keep reading to find all the essential details, including the official start time, the arena location, the live television channel, and your streaming options. When is Kentucky Wildcats vs Santa Clara Broncos? What Time Does it Start? The first-round matchup between the Kentucky Wildcats and the Santa Clara Broncos takes place on March 20, 2026. Tip-off is officially set for 12:15 PM ET. The game will be played in the local Central Time Zone at 11:15 AM CT. Where is Kentucky vs Santa Clara? This postseason game takes place at the Enterprise Center in St. Louis, Missouri. The venue serves as a neutral site for the opening weekend of the tournament. For administrative purposes, the Kentucky Wildcats are the designated home team. The Santa Clara Broncos will operate as the designated away team for this contest. How Can I Watch the Kentucky vs Santa Clara Matchup? Fans planning to view the game between the Kentucky Wildcats and the Santa Clara Broncos can find the live television broadcast on CBS. The CBS network provides full national coverage of this scheduled Midwest Region contest. How Can I Stream the Kentucky vs Santa Clara Game? Because the game is broadcast on CBS, you can stream the matchup live using Paramount+. This branded streaming platform provides access to local CBS broadcasts for subscribers on the appropriate premium tier. If you do not use Paramount+, several other major live TV streaming services carry local CBS stations. You can watch the game using platforms like YouTube TV, Hulu + Live TV, FuboTV, Sling, and DirecTV Stream. Just verify that your specific subscription package includes your local CBS affiliate.
